 Closings and Delays 2 weather alerts in effect FIRST ALERT: First potential snowfall arrives tonight 
 By Connor Thompson Published : Nov. 12, 2026 at 4:12 AM EST | Updated : 18 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google Today: Cloudy with rain. Chance of rain 100%. Wind: NE 10-15 G30. High: 40-47. 
 Steady rain during the day (WBNG) Tonight: FIRST ALERT WEATHER DAY. Cloudy with rain to snow. Chance of precip 90%. Wind: NNW 5-10 G25. Low: 29-34. 
 Near freezing temperatures overnight (WBNG) Snow begins to taper Friday morning (WBNG) Friday: FIRST ALERT WEATHER DAY. Cloudy with snow showers. Chance of snow 60%. Wind: NNW 5-15 G25. High: 34-39. 
 Remaining cold Friday afternoon (WBNG) Friday Night: Cloudy and cold. Wind: NW 5-10. Low: 24-31. 
 Saturday: Cloudy and cold. Isolated snow showers. Chance of snow 30%. High: 38. Low: 33. 
 Sunday: Cloudy skies. High: 40. Low: 34. 
 Monday: Cloudy skies with decreasing clouds late. High: 42. Low: 29. 
 After a cold weekend, temperatures warm next week (WBNG) Tuesday: Mostly sunny. High: 47. Low: 30. 
 Wednesday: Mostly sunny. High: 51. Low: 31. 
 Forecast Discussion: 
 What to expect today and tomorrow (WBNG) A complex weather set will arrive today and continue as we head into the end of the workweek. An area of low pressure will slide south of the region, allowing for rain throughout the day. As we get into the late afternoon and early evening, an energy transfer will occur, with the energy from this low-pressure system going to a coastal low. This will allow for colder air to work in, allowing for a changeover to snow as we head into the evening. Rainfall totals will be between .50″ and 1″, with localized higher totals. There is still a lot of uncertainty with the amount of snowfall that we could see, but what we do know is that the best chance to see accumulations will be the higher elevations, with the valley potentially seeing a quick dusting. Those in the higher elevations could see upwards of 1″-3″. Temperatures during the day will be in the mid-40s, while overnight lows fall to near freezing. 
 Some spots could see upwards of an inch of rain (WBNG) Rain changes over to snow early this evening (WBNG) Not a lot of snow expected (WBNG) Friday shows snow showers that will taper as we head into the afternoon. It will be cold and breezy, with highs in the mid-30s, and gusts nearing 25 MPH. To account for the risk of the first accumulating snow, tonight and Friday are FIRST ALERT WEATHER DAYS . 
 The weekend will start off cold and cloudy, with Saturday seeing highs in the upper 30s. A few lake-effect snow showers are possible, mainly in the morning. Sunday will be cloudy, with highs nearing 40. 
 Monday will see cloudy skies for most of the day, before high pressure builds in during the afternoon, allowing for clearing skies. Highs will be in the low 40s. Tuesday and Wednesday will see mostly sunny skies as high pressure settles overhead. Highs on both days will be in the upper 40s and lower 50s.
